Ulster Unionists want the election to be a referendum on how the Renewable Heat Incentive debacle was handled.

summary: Steroids and medicines with an estimated street value of some 2m euros (Â£1.7m) have been seized in Donegal.
lead: More than 60,000 vials, said to contain anabolic steroids, were recovered in an operation by Garda (Irish police), customs and a medicine watchdog.

summary: Sinn FÃ©in leader Gerry Adams has said there is "a need to be open and imaginative" on new constitutional arrangements.
lead: He welcomed Taoiseach (Irish prime minister) Enda Kenny's comments on a possible referendum on Irish unity.

summary: Morecambe must not get carried away despite sitting top of League Two, says Shrimps boss Jim Bentley.
lead: The Shrimps lost their opening game of the season at newly-promoted Grimsby but then knocked Championship side Rotherham out of the EFL Cup 5-4 and have won three straight league games.

summary: Some demands set by four Arab states on Qatar in return for lifting sanctions will be "difficult to meet", US Secretary of State Rex Tillerson says.
lead: However, Mr Tillerson said the proposals provided a basis for dialogue leading to a solution of the crisis.

summary: UKIP ex-deputy chairwoman Suzanne Evans says she has given up hope of becoming the party's next leader - but insists she will not "give up" on UKIP.
lead: Ms Evans, who is currently suspended from UKIP, said she would "very much like" to run but a "handful of people at the top" had ensured she could not.

summary: A court in the Indian capital has formally charged a driver of the Uber web-based taxi firm with the rape and kidnapping of a passenger last month.
lead: Shiv Kumar Yadav has also been charged with "criminal intimidation" of the 26-year-old woman, reports said.

summary: Standing hand-in-hand like theatre actors at their curtain call, Wales' players were met with a spine-tingling rendition of the national anthem from their fans following their European Championship semi-final defeat by Portugal.
lead: This was the end of the road for Wales in France but the 'Red Wall' - as Wales' players have dubbed their supporters - was still roaring its encouragement at full volume.

summary: Ferguslie Park in Paisley has been identified as the area of Scotland with the greatest level of deprivation.
lead: It is the second successive time the area has been at the bottom of the Scottish Index of Multiple Deprivation (SIMD), which is published every four years.

summary: Coleraine rower Joel Cassells and Great Britain team-mate Sam Scrimgeour remain on course to defend their lightweight pairs world title after winning their semi-final in Rotterdam on Thursday.
lead: Cassells, 22, and Scrimgeour clocked six minutes and 29.63 seconds to finish ahead of Denmark and China.

summary: Former Kilmarnock winger Chris Johnston has become the third player to sign for Dumbarton this summer after leaving relegated Raith Rovers.
lead: The 22-year-old, who has signed a one-year contract, joins defender Craig Barr and striker Mark Stewart at the Scottish Championship club.

summary: James Milner's late penalty gave Liverpool a hard-fought victory over Swansea, increasing the scrutiny on Swans boss Francesco Guidolin.
lead: Leroy Fer gave the hosts a first-half lead when he steered the ball home from close range at the back post after Baston Borja's knockdown from a corner.

summary: Scottish rugby suffered two body blows this week and, rather like boxer Ricky Burns who "drew" with his opponent after getting one heck of a hiding from opponent Raymundo Beltran, it's a little battered, a little broken and in need of time off the canvas.
lead: It's hard to tell which blow took us more by surprise, the first ever positive steroids test in the history of Scottish rugby, or the fact that  and think it's unfair that so many Scottish, Welsh and Irish teams qualify for the Heineken Cup from a league without relegation.

summary: The three-day TRNSMT music festival in Glasgow is to start later with a Friday line-up of acts including Radiohead and Belle and Sebastian.
lead: Doors to the event at Glasgow Green will open at 14:00.

summary: The US has warned North Korea to refrain from "irresponsible provocation" after the communist state said its main nuclear facility had resumed normal operations.
lead: The reactor at Yongbyon has been the source of plutonium for North Korea's nuclear weapons programme.

summary: A man has been arrested on suspicion of conspiracy to murder after pieces of human bones were found by detectives investigating the death of a man 25 years ago.
lead: Andrew Bedford, 27, from Huntingdon in Cambridgeshire, was last seen in September 1990.

summary: Picture the scene inside the BBC 5 live studio: a millionaire owner of a now managerless Super League club, a highly rated out-of-work coach keen for a return to the sport and an iconic player from a rival club that the owner wants to sign.
lead: "Did you set this up?" Salford City Reds owner Dr Marwan Koukash asked, at the start of the station's rugby league hour this week.

summary: Ireland eased to seven-wicket win over Zimbabwe to top their Women's World Twenty20 qualifying group and set up a semi-final against Scotland.
lead: The Joyce twins starred as the Irish made it three wins out of three in Bangkok on Tuesday.

summary: The daughter of a man who died after a hospital failed it its "duty of care" said lessons have not been learned.
lead: Colchester Hospital was rated as inadequate after a recent Care Quality Commission (CQC) inspection found it was relying on "unsuitable" agency staff.

summary: Great Britain's Mark Cavendish is third after day one of the men's omnium as he aims for his first Olympic Games medal.
lead:
Media playback is not supported on this device
Cavendish, who has won 30 stages at the Tour de France, came sixth in the first of six events - the scratch race.

summary: The Northern Ireland health service is to receive an extra £72m to help deal with pressures in the service.
lead: Finance Minister Máirtín Ó Muilleoir made the announcement as part of a reallocation of funds known as a monitoring round.

summary: The Winklevoss brothers have re-started their long-running legal dispute with Facebook and its boss Mark Zuckerberg.
lead: Just days after dropping a supreme court action, the twins filed a fresh lawsuit against the company.

summary: A 14-year-old boy has been left with "life-threatening" injuries after being knocked down by a car.
lead: The teenage pedestrian was knocked down by a Ford Focus in Oldgate Lane, Thrybergh, Rotherham, on Saturday, said South Yorkshire Police.

summary: Chapman Pincher was known as "the lone wolf of Fleet Street".
lead: As defence correspondent of the Daily Express he beat his rivals to a string of scoops.

summary: Birmingham City have signed Dundee forward Greg Stewart on a three-year deal for a fee believed to be around £500,000.
lead: He had rejected a move to Birmingham on Wednesday but has now agreed personal terms and passed his medical.

summary: A former soldier who agreed to obtain information from an army barracks for a newspaper will not face a trial, the Crown Prosecution Service has said.
lead: The former private, who is in her 20s, has accepted a conditional caution for misconduct in a public office.

summary: Inspectors have called for major improvements at two privately-run elderly care homes after finding problems during recent visits.
lead: The Care Inspectorate gave Nithsdale House in Pollokshields, Glasgow, a score of one - the lowest possible - across three areas examined.

summary: Four men were arrested in north London when police found a gun, a sword and a knife in the car they were travelling in.
lead: Officers were called to Derby Road, Enfield at 15:30 GMT on Saturday after reports of a gun being seen in a car.

summary: An estimated 63,000 properties in north Lancashire were hit by a power cut, Electricity North West has said.
lead: The company said Lancaster's Caton Road substation went offline at 11:00 BST, leaving parts of the city and nearby Morecambe and Carnforth without power.

summary: Lord Derby has won a key High Court stage of his fight to build 400 homes on his land.
lead: The plans for the development on the Hatchfield Farm estate in Newmarket, Suffolk, had been approved by Forest Heath District Council.

summary: Shopkeepers near the Isle of Wight's troubled new "floating bridge" have asked councillors to consider compensating them for loss of business.
lead: The call was made at a scrutiny meeting of the council to discuss the problems surrounding the new vessel.

summary: French side Lille have exercised their option to sign Naim Sliti on a permanent deal when his loan move from second-tier side Red Star expires this summer.
lead: The 24-year-old Tunisia international, who initially joined Lille on a season-long loan last summer, has agreed a three-year contract with Les Dogues.

summary: Children across Britain linked up with Tim Peake on the International Space Station yesterday for a big question and answer session.
lead:
3 February 2016 Last updated at 08:07 GMT
The British astronaut has been up there for six weeks, but took time out to speak to children and share some experiments.

summary: World champion cyclist Martyn Irvine has been named the 2013 BBC Northern Ireland Sports Personality of the Year.
lead:
Media playback is not supported on this device
The Newtownards man became the first Irish cyclist to win a world track title in 117 years when he triumphed in the scratch race in Belarus.

summary: A civilian cargo aircraft has landed safely after being escorted into Prestwick Airport in Ayrshire after suffering technical problems with its communications equipment.
lead: A major emergency had been declared at the airport after the Italian C-27J aircraft lost communication.

summary: Police have been given more time to question five men arrested on suspicion of terrorism offences.
lead: Bomb disposal officers were sent to Birmingham's Lee Bank area on Friday and nearby roads were closed and cordoned off.

summary: Euro 2016 will be contested by 24 teams over 30 days at 10 different venues in France.
lead:
Media playback is not supported on this device
The tournament kicks off with France playing Romania on Friday, 10 June and the final will take place at the Stade de France in Paris on 10 July.

summary: BBC Sport is showing live coverage of the EuroBasket warm-up game between Great Britain and Greece at the Copper Box in London on Saturday 19 August.
lead: Coverage will be on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport website and app.

summary: Australia weathered a Welsh storm to win World Cup Pool A with a 15-6 victory at Twickenham.
lead: Wales paid a high price for failing to make their extra numbers count when the Wallabies were reduced to 13 men for seven minutes in the second half.

summary: Josh Strauss believes Vern Cotter's impending departure will provide added motivation for Scotland to have a successful Six Nations.
lead: Cotter will leave the Scotland job and be replaced by Glasgow boss Gregor Townsend at the end of the season.

summary: Ex-CIA Director David Petraeus has told the BBC that Islamic State militants can only be defeated through a dual military and political approach.
lead: "Industrial-strength" extremists cannot be dealt with "just with force of arms", he said in a rare interview.

summary: More than 13,000 email addresses have been stolen from Edinburgh city council's database following a "malicious cyber attack".
lead: The breach happened 10 days ago when the council's website service provider, which is based in England, was targeted by hackers.

summary: Rebels say they have begun a new battle in north-western Syria in response to alleged truce violations by the army.
lead: A statement announced the formation of a joint operations room following what it said was an increase in attacks on residential areas and displaced people.

summary: The photo sharing service Instagram announced it will start placing ads in US users photo streams in a posting on its website.
lead: "We have big ideas for the future, and part of making them happen is building Instagram into a sustainable business," it said.

summary: Actor Michael C Hall is to perform a tribute to David Bowie at this week's Mercury Music Prize ceremony.
lead: The star of TV series Dexter and Six Feet Under, Hall played the lead role in Bowie's musical Lazarus, which premiered shortly before his death.

summary: A former Metropolitan Police officer has been found not guilty of sexually assaulting a teenage boy in the back of a police van nearly 30 years ago.
lead: Gurpal Virdi, 56, of Hounslow, west London, was acquitted by the jury at Southwark Crown Court.

summary: Welsh Secretary Alun Cairns has rejected calls for a "softer" Brexit after the general election result led to a hung parliament.
lead: Mr Cairns said it would be "completely wrong" to remain in the EU's single market as both major UK parties told voters they wanted to leave.

summary: Relatives of the 96 people who died at Hillsborough have told the home secretary they want a "Hillsborough Law" to compel public officials to tell the truth at inquiries.
lead: They held private meetings with Theresa May in the wake of the Hillsborough inquests, which ended in April.

summary: Internet trolls who create derogatory hashtags or doctored images to humiliate others could face prosecution in England and Wales.
lead: Inciting people to harass others online, known as virtual mobbing, could also result in court action, under new Crown Prosecution Service guidance.

summary: The day 12-year-old Faizan Fayaz Dar died, he woke up in the morning in his hilltop home in Budgam in Indian-administered Kashmir, had a cup of salted tea, recited the Koran and pottered around in the kitchen where his mother prepared breakfast for the family.
lead: His grandmother offered him a plate of grapes, but she doesn't remember whether Faizan had it.

summary: An elderly woman has died after being hit by a tipper truck.
lead: North Wales Police were called to the incident involving a silver Ford Transit truck in Nantlle Road, Talysarn, Gwynedd, on Friday afternoon.

summary: Four foreign-owned firms are competing to run train services in Wales and create the £600m South Wales Metro.
lead: Bids have been submitted by Abellio, Arriva, KeolisAmey and MTR for the next Wales and Borders franchise.

summary: Veteran broadcaster Robbie Shepherd is leaving BBC Radio Scotland's Take the Floor after 35 years this weekend.
lead: The 80-year-old, a champion of the Doric dialect, was a compere and producer of variety shows before branching out into broadcasting.

summary: Accrington Stanley manager John Coleman has criticised the Football League for allowing Carlisle United to move their home games because of flooding.
lead: Following flooding at Brunton Park, Carlisle have three 'home' fixtures at neutral grounds and beat Notts County at Preston's Deepdale on Saturday.

summary: Two Manchester United fans spent Friday night undetected in an Old Trafford toilet in an attempt to see Saturday's Premier League game against Arsenal.
lead: The supporters had been on a stadium tour but managed to cut themselves off from the remainder of the party.

summary: Accrington Stanley secured a dramatic late victory over Championship side Preston North End to seal their place in the second round of the EFL Cup.
lead: The hosts led when Ben Richards-Everton volleyed home but Jordan Hugill slotted in to equalise for the visitors.

summary: An electrician whose £200 worth of tools were mistakenly sold for £1 in a charity shop has had them returned.
lead: Andrew Bickel, 39, was fixing a light at the Catwel shop in Cardiff two weeks ago when he nipped out to his van and returned to find his tools were gone.

summary: Laura Muir says she'll be "gutted" to miss April's Commonwealth Games.
lead:
Media playback is not supported on this device
Muir told BBC Scotland her veterinary medicine studies will mean she will not be with the Scotland team at next year's event on Australia's Gold Coast.

summary: Southend United will give striker Nile Ranger a chance to relaunch his career when he is released from prison.
lead: The former Newcastle striker, 26, was jailed for eight months in May after admitting online banking fraud.

summary: Books of condolence have opened for Sir Terry Wogan, as his breakfast show successor Chris Evans paid tribute on air to "radio's Eric Morecambe".
lead: The veteran broadcaster died of cancer on Sunday at the age of 77.

summary: First Minister Nicola Sturgeon has called for "cast iron assurances" jobs will not be lost at Clyde shipyards because of contract delays.
lead: Unions at BAE Systems have warned of possible delays to funding for the Royal Navy's new frigates.

summary: Republican presidential hopefuls Ted Cruz and Marco Rubio have unleashed a barrage of attacks on front-runner Donald Trump in the last debate before next Tuesday's pivotal US primaries.
lead: Immigration, healthcare and outreach to Latino voters dominated the debate, which disintegrated into long periods of shouting and personal insults.

summary: So Ukraine confounded the bookmakers and Eurovision commentators who had been convinced that Russia - or possibly Australia - would win.
lead: Russia's CG effects and the brilliance of Australia's singing were not enough to defeat jazz artist Jamala.

summary: Lifeguards will patrol a popular beach on the South Coast this summer after seven men drowned last year.
lead: The patrols at Camber Sands in East Sussex will be funded with Â£51,000 allocated by Rother District Council as part of its annual budget.

summary: Partick Thistle captain Abdul Osman says the players are praying manager Alan Archibald stays at the club for another season.
lead: Archibald was on Swindon Town's managerial shortlist last season and has been linked with other vacancies.

summary: Ten youths have been arrested by Canadian police on suspicion of planning to travel to Iraq and Syria to join Islamic State.
lead: All 10 had their passports confiscated after they were detained at Montreal's Trudeau International Airport at the weekend.

summary: League Two side York City have signed Hull City midfielder Matt Dixon on an 18-month deal.
lead: The 21-year-old made his debut for the Tigers in the League Cup first-round tie against Accrington Stanley in August.

summary: Up to £500m could be recovered from overseas visitors and migrants using the NHS every year, ministers believe.
lead: An independent report commissioned by the Department of Health estimated these groups cost the NHS £2bn a year.

summary: Belfast Giants remain within four points of Elite League leaders Cardiff Devils after earning a 5-1 Boxing Day away win over Braehead Clan.
lead: Colin Shields put Belfast ahead before Scott Aarssen levelled late in the first period.

summary: BBC Rewind looks at the history of the Flying Scotsman as it prepares to return to the railways.
lead:
25 February 2016 Last updated at 10:01 GMT
Having undergone significant restoration, it will make its first journey in ten years along the East Coast mainline.

summary: A man who claimed he was abused at an East Yorkshire Catholic school has lost a legal action for compensation.
lead: He is one of 249 men suing the Catholic Church over alleged historical sexual abuse at St William's residential school in Market Weighton.
